function_signature: def sliding_window_modexp(base: int, exponent: int, modulus: int, window_size: int) -> int
expected_pass_rate: >= 0.7 (18 test cases in all; the main metric is task_success, scored 0 or 1 for the whole task: it is 1 only if no blocking failure occurs and every functional case passes — the registered process and performance cases are excluded from the functional set but block on failure; the pass-rate threshold on the left and the per-case pass rate are recorded as diagnostics only)
constraints: Using pow(base, exponent, modulus) directly is not allowed

The steps of the sliding window algorithm:
   a) precompute base^1, base^3, ..., base^(2^k-1) mod modulus (odd powers only)
   b) scan the binary representation of exponent from the high bits down
   c) on a 0: result = result^2 mod modulus, the window slides 1 bit
   d) on a 1: find the longest window (at most k bits, ending in a 1) → result = result^(2^wlen) * precomputed[win_val] mod modulus
precomputed uses the recurrence base^(odd)=base^(odd-2)*base^2 mod modulus
The caller guarantees exponent >= 0, modulus > 0 and window_size >= 1 (these are input preconditions and the implementation need not validate them)
source: 《密码工程》(Cryptographic Engineering, in Chinese) Ch.4 §3; HAC §14.6.1 (Sliding Window); Kocher CRYPTO 1996
author: Liang Jing
